articles.text:
AS THE new dispensation in Dhaka comes under increasing criticism for attacks on minorities in the wake of the regime change, the plight of the 19 minority MPs of Sheikh Hasina's Awami League is a telling story. After the dissolution of Parliament, three of them were senttojail; most of the ahersare in hiding, in and outside the country. Among those sent to jail were veteran Awami League leaders and former Cabinet Ministers: Ramesh Chandra Sen, Narayan Chandra, and Sadhan Chandra Majumdar. Awami League leaders The Indian Express spoke to say there were around 2,000 incidents of arson, loot and buming involving the minorities (Hindus, Buddhists and Christians) between August 5 and August 20, 2024 and "scattered attacks" were still taking placeeveryday. According to Pankaj Nath, three-time MP from Barishal constituency (a former general secretary of the Bangladesh Awami Volunteers League, he fought the 2024 elections as an independent), almost all minority MPs have witnessed attacks on their properties and have had their hank accounts frozen,

Nath's residence in Dhaka was among them and while he himself is underground, his family, wo, is "taking precautions" moving from "place to place" in Bangladesh His personal anguish continues ashe could not attend the last nites of his mother when she passed away on December 28. CON TINUEDON PAGE2

BACKING THE H-1B visa pro-

month, US President Donald

“very competent” and “great”
people, and this is possible
through this visa programme.
Speaking at the White House
during a joint news conference
with Oracle CTO Larry Ellison,
Softbank CEO Masayoshi Son

like both sides of the argument,
but I also like very competent
peoplecoming int our country,

evenif that involves them train-
ing and helping other people
who maynot have the qualifica-
tions they do. But I don't want to
stop — and I'm not just talking
about engineers, I'm talking
about people at all levels.”

articles.headline_raw: On new ISRO chief’s table: 100th launch this month, PSLV built by pvt sector
articles.body_raw:
ANCHOR

ANONNADUTT
NEW DELHI, JANUARY 23

AFTER THE historic space dock-
ing experiment, the Indian Space
Research Organisation (ISRO) is
getting ready for another mile-
stone, its 100th launch, that is set
to happen at the end of the
month, This would be the first
mission to be launched under
the leadership of new ISRO
Chairman V Narayanan who

took charge earlier this month.
“The 100th launch of ISRO is
planned for later this month. It
would launch the NVS-02 satel-
lite, which issecond of thesecond-
generation navigation satellites
being deployed for India’s NaviC
constellation,” NarayanantoldThe
Indian Express in aninterview.
NaviC, or Navigation with
Indian Constellation, is the oper-
ational name for the Indian
Regional Navigation Satellite
System, IRNSS, which is a con-
stellation of seven satellites pro-
viding positioning, navigation
and timing services over the
Indian region and its immediate

neighbourhood. The satellites
are deployed in the geasynchro-
nous orbits.
First launched in July 2013,
the IRNSS constellation wascom-
pleted in 2018, but not all the
satellites have been functional.
The first set of satellites are now
being replaced with NVS series
of satellites that have more ad-
vanced features, and carry a
moreaccurate Rubidium atomic
clock for precise positioning and
navigation. The first satellite in
thisseries NVS-01 was launched
in May 2023. NVS-02is the sec-
ond in the series. These second-
generation satellites havea mis-

sion life of 12 years.
Narayanan said the launchof
NVS-02 was another important
step forward towards quick
commercidlisation and adoption
of India's ownindigenously-built
navigation system.
He said another important
event he was looking forward to
in the immediate future was the
launch of private ly-built PSLV
rocket. PSLV is ISRO's most pro-
lific and reliable rocket, having
made more than 60 flights since
itsinduction in 1994. ISROis now
getting the private industry to
manufacture this rocket.
‘The PSLV completely manu-

factured by the industry is inthe
final phase. We will soon see a
launch of that. We are going tw see
increased participation of the pri-
vate sector in space. The Prime
Minister has rolled out reformsin
the space sector, and itisnow our
responsibility to hand-hold the
private industry,” Narayanan said.
The ISRO Chairman also
spoke about other major under-
takings of the space agency, in-
cluding the development of
NGLV, the next generation launch
vehicle with which he himself
has been closely associated, and
the upcoming Gaganyaan and
Chandrayaan-4 missions.

“NGLY has a totally different
kind of capability (compared to
ISRO's current rockets). It will be
91 metreshigh almostastall as a
30-storey building, asagainst43
metres for (GSLV) Mk Ill rocket. It
will have the capability ofcarry-
ing 30,000 kgs tolow earth orbit.
Our current capacity with the
Bahubali Mk Ill rocket is only
around 8,500 kgs. When you
look at our future programmes,
we will need to have very high
capability rockets,” he said.
CONTINUEDON PAGE2
